newsitem.title: THAILAND: Chavalit says completes new Thai cabinet lineup.
newsitem.headline: Chavalit says completes new Thai cabinet lineup.

text.p: Thailand's premier-designate Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Thursday he and his five coalition partners had completed the lineup of the new cabinet and were nearly ready to present it to the king for royal approval.
Chavalit made the announcement after receiving the final list of 11 cabinet members that fall under the quota of the second largest coalition partner, the Chart Pattana Party (CPP).
"The complete cabinet list is in my hands and I think it will take another day for final checks before we present it to the king, (for royal approval)," Chavalit told reporters.

Chavalit's New Aspiration Party (NAP) won two more seats than the rival Democrat Party in the November 17 general election and became the core of a six-party coalition that holds 221 seats in the 393-seat lower house.
The NAP is set to assume 27 of the 49 cabinet posts.

Since the election, the NAP and its coalition partners have been embroiled in fierce wrangling over how to share the various ministries. Most of the delay was caused by differences between the NAP and CPP over how to divide the economic ministries.
Chavalit said his government would give top priority to boosting Thailand's sagging economy.

He said he would appoint two non-elected experts to head the economic efforts. Economist Amnuay Viravan would be finance minister and Narongchai Akrasanee, the chairman of Thailand's General Finance and Securities Plc, would be commerce minister.
Chavalit, a former army chief and defence minister, is to take the defence portfolio while NAP secretary-general Snoh Thiengthong was set to become interior minister.
The Ministry of the Interior deals with all levels of social welfare and security issues, overseeing a police force of more than 200,000 and supervising all the provincial governors.
The CPP was assigned to oversee ministries dealing with infrastructure -- transport & communication and industry -- and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The smaller parties in the coalition -- Social Action, Prachakorn Thai, Seritham and Moun Chon -- were assigned the ministries dealing with social welfare, public health, science and technology and the environment.
Prachakorn Thai has been handed the tough task of solving Bangkok's notorious traffic congestion.
Chavalit, who has been officially appointed the country's 22nd prime minister, and his cabinet are to be sworn in by King Bhumibol Adulyadej on December 1.
